COND-C02-COVIDOUT-2022: The COVID-OUT randomized placebo-controlled trial evaluated metformin, ivermectin and fluvoxamine for acute COVID-19.
People with acute COVID-19; the existing ivermectin outcome record identifies the 808 participants in its relevant comparison. This is not a count of participants across every trial arm.
The ivermectin comparison did not demonstrate a reduction in the composite of hypoxemia, emergency care, hospitalization or death.

The result concerns a specific acute-treatment composite. It does not establish efficacy for cancer or for treating established Long COVID, and related COVID-OUT reports are not additional independent trials.
P-D08-ACTIV6-2023: ACTIV-6 compared a six-day higher-dose ivermectin schedule with placebo for time to sustained recovery.
Outpatients with mild to moderate COVID-19.
The tested schedule did not shorten sustained recovery.
This randomized clinical result does not support a recovery benefit from the tested regimen. It addresses patients and recovery directly, unlike cell-culture antiviral experiments.
P-D08-ANTIVIRAL-2023: Laboratory experiments examined whether membrane effects could explain ivermectin’s in vitro antiviral activity.
Cell-culture and membrane models, rather than patients receiving a COVID-19 treatment.
Antiviral effects occurred at concentrations above reported toxic clinical concentrations and were associated with nonspecific membrane effects.
The exposure and membrane findings limit translation from antiviral activity in vitro to a usable human treatment. They do not establish that higher dosing would provide clinical benefit.
P-D08-OVARIAN-2009: Cell-culture experiments examined PAK1 activity and growth after ivermectin exposure.
Human ovarian cancer and NF2-deficient schwannoma cell models.
The reported findings link PAK1 inhibition with suppressed cell growth.
The experiment supports a mechanistic hypothesis in these cell models. It did not measure patient survival or symptoms and cannot supply a clinical cancer-benefit estimate.
P-D08-GBM-2016: Preclinical experiments examined mitochondrial respiration, oxidative stress and tumor growth under ivermectin exposure.
Glioblastoma cells and experimental tumor models.
Mitochondrial respiration inhibition and increased oxidative stress accompanied growth suppression.
The findings identify an experimental growth-inhibition mechanism. Their presence in tumor models does not demonstrate a safe or effective glioblastoma treatment in people.
P-D08-BREAST-2016: Experiments examined PAK1 degradation, Akt/mTOR signaling and autophagy after ivermectin exposure.
Breast cancer cell and animal models.
PAK1 degradation and reduced Akt/mTOR signaling were associated with growth-arresting autophagy.
The study links a pathway change to an experimental growth effect. It does not establish improved clinical outcomes or a human breast-cancer dosing schedule.
P-D08-CRC-2014: Cell and animal experiments tested WNT-TCF pathway responses and tumor growth, including pathway-rescue and comparison models.
WNT-dependent human cancer models, including colorectal cancer cells and mouse xenografts.
Forcing TCF signaling back on rescued cells from some low-concentration effects. Ivermectin inhibited TCF-dependent xenografts but not the TCF-independent comparison model.

The rescue and comparison experiments strengthen a specific mechanistic explanation. Tumor biology, exposure and formulation still limit clinical translation; this study is not an independent randomized patient trial.
P-D08-HCC-2022: The original report described preclinical experiments combining ivermectin with sorafenib. The report is retracted.
Hepatocellular carcinoma experimental models, rather than a clinical patient comparison.
No efficacy conclusion is retained from this retracted report.
The report remains traceable for source-integrity context only. Its reported effects cannot support a benefit grade, a combination mechanism or a treatment recommendation.
